Sparse linear solvers

Source: R/sparse-solvers.R
solve_linear_system.Rd

solve_linear_system() solves A x = b for a sparse matrix and reports diagnostics. linear_solver() prepares a reusable solver (for example a Cholesky factorization) for repeated right-hand sides, as in time stepping.

Usage

solve_linear_system(
  A,
  b,
  method = c("auto", "cholesky", "lu", "cg", "bicgstab", "gmres"),
  tol = 1e-10,
  maxit = 10 * length(b),
  preconditioner = "jacobi",
  restart = 50,
  x0 = NULL
)

linear_solver(
  A,
  method = c("auto", "cholesky", "lu", "cg", "bicgstab", "gmres"),
  tol = 1e-10,
  maxit = NULL,
  preconditioner = "jacobi",
  restart = 50
)

Arguments

A

A square sparse matrix (Matrix class) or base matrix.

b

Right-hand side vector, or a matrix of right-hand sides (one per column; direct methods solve all columns with one factorization).

method

Solver, see Details.

tol

Relative residual tolerance for iterative methods.

maxit

Maximum iterations for iterative methods.

preconditioner

"jacobi", "ssor", "none", a function(r), or a preconditioner from multigrid_preconditioner().

restart

Restart length for GMRES.

x0

Initial guess for iterative methods.

Value

solve_linear_system() returns a list with x and info, a list of diagnostics (method, status, residual, relative_residual, iterations, tol, n, nnz, symmetric, time). linear_solver() returns a list with a function solve(b) and info.

Details

Methods:

  • "auto": sparse Cholesky (CHOLMOD through Matrix) for symmetric matrices, falling back to sparse LU when the factorization shows the matrix is not positive definite; sparse LU for nonsymmetric matrices.

  • "cholesky": sparse Cholesky; fails for matrices that are not symmetric positive definite.

  • "lu": sparse LU (any nonsingular matrix).

  • "cg": preconditioned conjugate gradients (symmetric positive definite matrices only).

  • "bicgstab", "gmres": preconditioned BiCGSTAB and restarted GMRES for general matrices.

Iterative methods use Jacobi (diagonal) preconditioning by default; "ssor" is symmetric Gauss-Seidel (two sparse triangular solves per application, symmetric for symmetric matrices, so usable with CG); a multigrid_preconditioner() gives mesh-independent iteration counts on nested meshes; and any function(r) returning an approximation of A^{-1} r can be passed. Iterative methods iterate on the scaled system A y = b / max|b|, which avoids overflow and underflow. They report "converged" only when the true residual of the returned solution satisfies ||b - A x|| <= tol * ||b||, and "not converged" otherwise. Direct methods report the same relative residual, status "inaccurate" when the normwise backward error ||b - A x|| / (||A|| ||x|| + ||b||) exceeds 1e-8, and status "near-singular" when the ratio of the smallest to the largest pivot of the factorization is below about 2e-13. That ratio is a conditioning diagnostic: the matrix is singular or nearly singular to working precision, for example a stiffness matrix without boundary conditions. A system with no unknowns returns method "none". A small residual says the linear system was solved accurately; it says nothing about the discretization error of the PDE.

References

Saad, Y. (2003). Iterative Methods for Sparse Linear Systems, 2nd edition. SIAM.

Examples

V <- fe_space(pde_mesh_rectangle(nx = 8))
A <- assemble_matrix(V, "stiffness") + assemble_matrix(V, "mass")
b <- assemble_vector(V, 1)
s1 <- solve_linear_system(A, b)
s2 <- solve_linear_system(A, b, method = "cg", tol = 1e-12)
max(abs(s1$x - s2$x))
#> [1] 1.509903e-14
s2$info$iterations
#> [1] 23
